source.title: Grokking and epoch-wise double descent in quantum neural networks
source.authors: Daniel Pranjic; M. Roth; C. Tutschku

record.tranche_reason: The study empirically tests epoch-wise double descent using a two-qubit quantum neural network, a different model family and experimental setup from the original deep-network studies.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own test-error trajectory and final test-error comparisons under explicit weight-norm regularization. Depth-related grokking and generalization success rates are not rows for V1 because the study does not report test error as a function of model size. Values used to define phases or characterize trajectories are included only where they report outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study reports test error over training epochs for a two-qubit quantum neural network and labels the trajectory epoch-wise double descent. That bears on V2 in a new model family, so T3 fits better than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors also stress a late-stage generalization decay tied to weight-norm growth, and present it as the main reason for adding weak regularization. They also argue broad initialization with weight decay need not trap QNNs in barren plateaus.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a two-qubit variational quantum circuit over SU(4), a concentric-circles task, and long-duration training; it does not reproduce the original deep-network size, data, or epoch sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported grokking and generalization outcomes vary with circuit depth, learning rate, weight decay, initialization scale, and test-boundary distance epsilon. The study does not show that these settings change a quantitatively established epoch-wise double-descent peak.

fits_no_version.finding: Generalization success and grokking occurrence rise with circuit depth. For nl ≥ 7, all 128 runs generalize (Fig 3a).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overparameterizing QNNs via depth raises the probability of eventual generalization under grokking dynamics.

fits_no_version.finding: Unregularized deeper QNNs show late-stage generalization decay after grokking, with test error rising while training loss stays flat. Weak L2 regularization (λ=1e-4) suppresses this decay without changing τg/τf.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In deeper QNNs, explicit weight-norm regularization prevents post-grokking test-error decay without altering grokking timing.

record.problems: The main epoch-wise result is presented as one detailed training run, and its detailed description does not clearly report the intermediate test-error rise required for fall-rise-fall. The paper also reports final-error distributions over seeds but gives no CI, SD, or p-values in the text.

untested.parts: No test-error curve over model size or across an interpolation threshold. Depth is varied only for generalization success ratios.
How often the fall-rise-fall shape occurs across seeds is not quantified. The abstract says 'frequently', but no count is given.
No capacity-risk curve across model classes.
No effective-complexity measure is used to predict peak location.
No label-noise manipulation, no multiple peaks, and no test of whether tuned regularization removes the epoch-wise peak.

missing.what: The frequency of epoch-wise double descent (an intermediate rise in test error) across the 128-seed runs. The abstract says 'frequently', but no rate or figure is reported. If it exists, it should be a V2 row.
A readout of the Fig 2a test-error curve that shows whether any rise occurs between epochs 184 and 5477. The text says the curve is static.

record.verdict_notes: The paper's 'epoch-wise double descent' label rests on the abstract and the conceptual sketch in Fig 1b. The detailed results describe a fall, a plateau and a fall (grokking). The only clear rise reported is late-stage decay after generalization, which is the opposite ordering. The verdict is therefore limits_scope, not supports. Tranche changed from T2 to T3 because this is a new model family measured on the same quantity.

versions.untested_parts: No test-error curve over model size or interpolation threshold is reported.
The detailed trajectory is a single run in one two-qubit QNN setting; the reported description does not quantify a distinct intermediate test-error peak.
Training-set size is not varied to test whether more data raises test error.
The study does not compare a range of model classes or test a general capacity-risk curve.
The study does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak location across axes.
The study does not test noise-driven peaks, multiple descent peaks, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes the epoch-wise double-descent peak.
The study does not recount complexity using an effective number of parameters.

rows.subject: 2-qubit QNN parameterized over the complete SU(4) manifold
rows.operation_detail: Tracked test error across training epochs during one training run.
rows.value: Test error first falls to a local minimum of approximately 0.3; the detailed Results text says it remains static during the memorization phase, then drops to zero by the generalization transition at epoch 5477. The abstract describes degradation at a critical epoch before recovery.
rows.note: The paper calls the behavior epoch-wise double descent and describes two non-monotonous transitions, but its detailed account says test error is static through the memorization plateau and does not quantify a distinct intermediate rise. The abstract's description of degradation before recovery is not reconciled with that account. Training error falls below 0.1 at epoch 184; the memorization phase ends at epoch 3418.
rows.check: The state stands. Subsection 3.1 says test error falls to about 0.3, stays 'entirely static' through memorization, then drops to zero. No intermediate rise is reported in the text. Only the abstract asserts 'degrading at a critical epoch before recovering'. The curve reads as a two-step descent (grokking), not fall-rise-fall. It is a single run.

rows.subject: 2-qubit QNN parameterized over the complete SU(4) manifold
rows.operation_detail: Compared final test-error distributions after training with and without explicit weight-norm regularization.
rows.value: The study reports no perceptible divergence between regularized and unregularized results for shallow models (nl < 4).
rows.uncertainty: Final test-error distributions are shown; no CI, SD, or p-value is stated.
rows.note: This endpoint comparison reports regularization's effect on final test error, not the shape of test error over epochs.
rows.check: Unlinked is correct. This compares final test error with and without regularization in shallow models. It says nothing about the epoch-wise peak or a noise-driven peak.

rows.subject: 2-qubit QNN parameterized over the complete SU(4) manifold
rows.operation_detail: Compared final test-error distributions after training with and without explicit weight-norm regularization.
rows.value: Regularized runs converge overwhelmingly to final test error approximately zero; unregularized runs show significant variance, with a prominent cluster at high final test error.
rows.uncertainty: Final test-error distributions are shown; no CI, SD, or p-value is stated.
rows.note: The result concerns late-stage generalization preservation and does not establish whether the epoch-wise double-descent shape or its peak disappears.
rows.check: Unlinked is correct. The late-stage decay that regularization suppresses is a rise after the second descent. It is not the double-descent peak, so it does not bear on V6's claim that tuned regularization removes the peak.

relationships.condition: 3-layer SU(4) two-qubit QNN, single reported run (Fig 2a), concentric-circles task
relationships.reason: R1: test error falls to about 0.3, stays static, then drops to zero. The intermediate rise V2 requires is not reported in the results text; only the abstract claims a degradation. The shape resembles a grokking plateau more than fall-rise-fall.
relationships.display_finding: Test error fell to about 0.3, plateaued, then dropped to zero; the results description reported no intermediate rise despite the abstract claiming degradation.
